replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the essentials, and the evidence bears them out. The trip from Bishan to Kallang Wave Mall on 14 July 2026 was driven on an 11.18 km GPS trace against an 8.2 km booked optimal — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.3% — which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is established (rider's threshold claim accepted). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 175 fixes at the expected 10-second spacing, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so no independent corroboration beyond the trace is required (rider's POL-RD-07 claim accepted).

The deviation is nevertheless fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260714-031 closed Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00 that day; that is the road the booked optimal route traverses; the window covers the 08:07-08:36 trip with far more than the 15-minute buffer; and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor inside the advisory geometry and rejoining it afterwards. The justified excess is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so no excess remains and no distance or time refund arises (driver's exoneration claims accepted; the rider's alternative POL-RD-02 computation is moot because the closure excuses the whole excess).

The rider does not, however, pay for gantries she did not choose. Both CTE gantry lines on the fare breakdown — S$3.00 at CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) and S$1.00 at CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) — are flagged on_optimal_route false, and the optimal route carries no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand because the driver is not at fault, but off-route ERP is refunded as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at S$12.00. The four dollars are due back. The diversion was not rider-caused — the only message naming it, 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah', is the driver's, and the rider's 'ok' is an acknowledgement of a choice already announced, with waypoint_hint null on both messages — so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the refund (rider's POL-RD-04 claim accepted).

The two gantry lines are matched to the trace, so they are not phantom charges and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises (driver's claim accepted). The deviation is 36.3%, below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality marks, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed trips in 90 days, so no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern uplift or conduct referral is available either (driver's claim accepted). Nothing is recovered twice: POL-RD-09(1) would fold off-route ERP into any POL-RD-02 refund, but no POL-RD-02 refund is computed here, so the S$4.00 is a standalone correction paid once.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, their timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, every cited clause rests on a present artifact, and confidence sits above the 0.70 floor. Driver compensation is null — no compensation limb is engaged. Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of S$4.00 to the rider; the base, distance and time lines stand.
